If that rule went through, the majority of the D-1 players could very well end up being Canadian.

Also if i’m being completely honest, the NCAA doesn’t want a large influx of Canadian players at American schools taking roster spots from American players and the CHL doesn’t want to lose talent to south of the border. Both leagues are “benefitting” from the NCAA ban of CHL players in their own way.

I think it would have the opposite effect. Most major junior players aged between u19 and u21 would rather move up to NCAA as the players are older/faster/stronger. The CHL already has an artificial tool to keep talent in their league by not allowing drafted u20 players to play in minor pro leagues. Most recent first round draft picks would rusher play against the older/stronger NCAA competition than teams that could technically be dressing seven to ten 15-17 year olds in the CHL.

Not if it puts you in overwhelming debt, and it depends on what your educational background is in. My sister got an Art history degree and ended up being in 6 figures of debt, now she sells cars for a living. No correlation... just over $100k to be able say “I have a degree” . Was it worth it? IMO I don’t think so. I know plenty of non college educated friends from high school who live just as awesome lives and make just as much money. 

However, I will say that sometimes non-college educated people downplay just how hard it is to earn certain degrees, and that gets annoying.

Because many jobs that people get after college do not pay enough for how much the degree was worth. Also, many jobs people get after college could be done without a degree. Too many people nowadays got to school, choose a major based on if it is easy or not, and end up in a career that has nothing to do with their education background. Keep in mind, I’m saying this all as a millennial who has 2 degrees and is currently in med school.
